uncertainties: Band 1 cuts this heading off. The reading comes from the full image, and I can't tell whether סֵדֶר has a meteg (סֵֽדֶר).
This line is unpointed and set in a smaller, letter-spaced type.

blocks.text: רִבּוֹן הָעוֹלָמִים, בָּנֶיךָ בְּנֵי רְחוּמֶיךָ שָׂמוּ פְנֵיהֶם לְנֶגְדֶּךָ וּבָטְחוּ עַל רֹב חֲסָדֶיךָ וְשָׂמוּנִי שָׁלִיחַ לִתְקוֹעַ בְּשׁוֹפָר לְפָנֶיךָ כְּמוֹ שֶׁצִּוִּיתָנוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ. וְאַתָּה תִּזְכּוֹר לָהֶם זְכוּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלֵּךְ לְפָנֶיךָ וְהָיָה תָמִים, וּזְכוּת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ וַעֲקֵדָתוֹ כְּשֶׁנֶּעֱקַד עַל גַּב הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וּזְכוּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ אִישׁ תָּם יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים, וּזְכוּת שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה וְכָל־צַדִּיקֵי עוֹלָם וְתַעֲמוֹד מִכִּסֵּא הַדִּין וְתֵשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא הָרַחֲמִים כַּדָּבָר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
uncertainties: In פְנֵיהֶם I can't tell whether the pe has a dagesh.
Several words may carry a meteg that I can't resolve, for example בָּנֶֽיךָ, רְחוּמֶֽיךָ, יַֽעֲקֹב and וְאַֽהֲרֹן.
The full stop after בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ is printed as a raised dot.

blocks.text: עָלָה אֱלֹהִים בִּתְרוּעָה יְיָ בְּקוֹל שׁוֹפָר:
uncertainties: The divine name is printed as יְיָ. The verse runs inline inside the prayer and has no separate typographic marking.

blocks.text: וַאֲנִי יוֹדֵעַ בְּעַצְמִי שֶׁאֵינֶנִּי כְּדַי לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל עַצְמִי וְכָל־שֶׁכֵּן עַל אֲחֵרִים וְכָל־שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁאֵין בִּי לֹא דַעַת וְלֹא חָכְמָה לְכַוֵּן כַּוָּנוֹת הַתְּקִיעוֹת וְצֵרוּפֵי שְׁמוֹתֶיךָ הַקְּדוֹשִׁים, אֲבָל בָּטַחְתִּי בְּרַחֲמֶיךָ הָרַבִּים וְיָדַעְתִּי כִּי לֹא תְשִׁיבֵנִי רֵיקָם מִלְּפָנֶיךָ. וְאַתָּה בְּטוּבְךָ תְּעוֹרֵר רַחֲמֶיךָ
uncertainties: The vowel under the dalet of כְּדַי looks like a patah in band 2, but it could be a tsere (כְּדֵי).

blocks.text: וִיהִי נֹעַם אֲדֹנָי אֱלֹהֵינוּ עָלֵינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֵינוּ כּוֹנְנֵהוּ
uncertainties: אֲדֹנָי is spelled out in full here, not written as יְיָ. Only part of the verse is quoted, and it is woven into the prayer.

blocks.text: וּתְצָרֵף מַחֲשַׁבְתֵּנוּ הַטּוֹבָה לְמַעֲשֶׂה כְּאִלּוּ נִתְכַּוַּנּוּ בְּכָל כַּוָּנוֹת הַתְּקִיעוֹת וְיַעֲלוּ תְּקִיעוֹתֵינוּ לְעוֹרֵר רַחֲמֶיךָ וּתְרַחֵם עַל בָּנֶיךָ וְתַהֲפֹךְ לָהֶם עַל יְדֵי תְקִיעוֹת אֵלֶּה מִדַּת הַדִּין לְמִדַּת הַחֶסֶד וְהָרַחֲמִים וְתִכָּנֵס לָהֶם לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין, סְתוֹם וַחֲתוֹם פֶּה שָׂטָן וְאַל יַשְׂטִין עָלֵינוּ וּבְבוֹא תוֹכֵחָה לְנֶגְדֶּךָ שְׁמֵנוּ מִסִּפְרְךָ אַל תִּמַּח, וּכְתוֹב לְחַיִּים טוֹבִים כָּל בְּנֵי בְּרִיתֵנוּ:
uncertainties: The word is printed singular, מַחֲשַׁבְתֵּנוּ, not מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵינוּ. I can't tell whether it has a meteg (מַֽחֲשַׁבְתֵּנוּ).
In תִּמַּח there is a short horizontal stroke above the letters, probably a rafe or similar mark. I can't tell exactly which letter it sits over.
I can't tell whether כּוֹנְנֵהוּ in the previous block has a meteg.

blocks.text: יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי לְפָנֶיךָ יְיָ צוּרִי וְגֹאֲלִי,
uncertainties: וְגֹאֲלִי is written defectively (holam, no vav) as far as I can see. There may be a meteg on it.

blocks.text: Master of the worlds, Thy children, the children of Thy favourites, turn their face towards Thee and trust in Thy great mercy. They have appointed me to blow the Shofar before Thee, as Thou hast commanded us in Thy Torah. Remember unto them the merit of our father Abraham, who walked before Thee in perfection; the merit of our father Isaac and his readiness for sacrifice when he lay bound upon the altar; the merit of our father Jacob, the upright man who dwelt in tents, as well as the merit of Moses, Aaron, David, Solomon and all the righteous men of the world. Rise from the throne of justice and sit on the throne of compassion, as it is said: God has arisen at the Teruah, the Lord at the sound of the Shofar . . . I myself know that I am not worthy to pray for myself, let alone for others, all the more since I have neither the knowledge nor the wisdom to bear in mind the intentions underlying the Shofar sounds and their connections with Thy holy names. But I trust in Thy great compassion and know that Thou wilt not turn me away empty from before Thee. And Thou in Thy goodness dost arouse Thine own compassion. So let the favour of the Lord our God be upon us and as for the work of our hands, confirm it. Consider good intentions as if they had been deeds, as if we had kept in mind all the intentions underlying the Shofar sounds, in order that those sounds of ours may ascend to arouse Thy compassion so that Thou mayest take pity on Thy children, through these Shofar sounds, transform the attribute of justice into the attribute of kindness and compassion and deal indulgently with us. Close and seal Satan's mouth that he may not accuse us and when our reproach comes before Thee, do not blot out our name from Thy book. Inscribe all the children of our covenant for a good life. May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart find favour before thee, O Lord, my rock and my redeemer, Amen.
uncertainties: The English runs as one paragraph. The verse renderings (Ps 47:6, Ps 90:17, Ps 19:15) are embedded inline, so I did not split them out. 'before thee' near the end is lowercase in the source.
The ellipsis after 'Shofar' is printed as spaced dots ('. . .').
